claims.claim: ⚠️ **Children with mediastinal masses can deteriorate acutely and rapidly become critically unwell.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Mediastinal mass' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Mediastinal_mass/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A mediastinal mass on CXR requires urgent escalation to a tertiary paediatric hospital** — involve retrieval services and oncology promptly.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Mediastinal mass' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Mediastinal_mass/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ask about** noisy breathing (stridor or wheeze), **orthopnoea** (difficulty lying flat to sleep), bone pain, and collapse or dizziness.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Mediastinal mass' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Mediastinal_mass/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Let the child adopt a position of comfort. Do not force them to lie flat.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Mediastinal mass' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Mediastinal_mass/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine for stridor or wheeze** (airway obstruction) and for **pericardial effusion or tamponade**: distended neck veins, muffled heart sounds, low blood pressure.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Mediastinal mass' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Mediastinal_mass/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Look for SVC obstruction; test Pemberton's sign** by having the child lift both arms until they touch the sides of the face — positive if facial congestion, cyanosis and respiratory distress develop.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Mediastinal mass' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Mediastinal_mass/, retrieved 2026-09-23

The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Mediastinal mass' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Mediastinal_mass/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discuss with oncology before further bloods** to avoid repeat sampling; peripheral blood flow cytometry may be diagnostic.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Mediastinal mass' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Mediastinal_mass/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Lateral CXR** to locate the mass; **CT chest only if the child can lie flat comfortably**; urgent echocardiogram and cardiology opinion if available.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Mediastinal mass' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Mediastinal_mass/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Arrange urgent retrieval to a tertiary paediatric hospital**, discussed with PICU and oncology.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Mediastinal mass' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Mediastinal_mass/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Plan sedation, general anaesthesia and all invasive procedures carefully to minimise the risk of airway compromise.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Mediastinal mass' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Mediastinal_mass/, retrieved 2026-09-23

The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Mediastinal mass' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Mediastinal_mass/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not start corticosteroids without consulting oncology.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Mediastinal mass' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Mediastinal_mass/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Manage every child with a new or symptomatic mediastinal mass in a centre with paediatric intensive care**; discuss all children with a mediastinal mass with the local paediatric team.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Oncological emergencies: Mediastinal mass' (Last updated December 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Oncological_emergencies__Mediastinal_mass/, retrieved 2026-09-23
